title: Musée d’Orsay: Masterpieces
subtitle: Funerals, floorboards and card games become substantial subjects in these twenty paintings.
introduction:
Courbet's village funeral stretches across a canvas nearly seven metres wide. The size matters: a local community occupies the kind of space traditionally granted to grand historical or religious events. Elsewhere in this selection, workers kneel over floorboards, dancers wait between exercises and two men attend to a game of cards.

These paintings do not all make the same argument about modern life. Manet tests the conventions of the nude; Whistler emphasises an arrangement of tones; Cézanne makes a table's structure uncertain. What connects them here is the attention given to subjects and decisions that a hierarchy of grand themes could overlook. The useful question is what each painting asks an ordinary action, object or pose to carry.
visitNote: Consult the Musée d’Orsay's current collection information for gallery locations and loans. The sequence here follows subjects and comparisons, not a walking route.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition places works by Monet, Renoir, Degas and their contemporaries in the setting of the early Impressionist exhibitions. The Met provides the catalogue online.

works.title: Olympia
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Olympia. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The flowers arrive, but the woman's attention is directed out of the painting. That division gives the reclining pose an alertness absent from the idea of a sleeping Venus. Manet painted a contemporary sex worker, retaining a composition associated with idealised nudes while withholding its mythological excuse. Painted in 1863, the work caused a scandal when exhibited at the Salon in 1865.

works.title: Luncheon on the Grass
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Le Déjeuner sur l’herbe. Image credit: Édouard Manet; Self-photographed. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Le_D%C3%A9jeuner_sur_l%27herbe_-_%C3%89douard_Manet.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The nude woman and the two dressed men do not seem to belong to the same social occasion. Manet makes no effort to resolve the discrepancy through mythology. Yet the composition draws on older art, including a group derived from Raphael through an engraving. Rejected by the Salon jury, the painting appeared at the Salon des Refusés in 1863: its challenge depended partly on familiar conventions put to unfamiliar use.

works.title: A Burial at Ornans
works.credit: Gustave Courbet. A Burial at Ornans. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: At 6.68 metres wide, this village funeral occupies space usually reserved for elevated historical or religious subjects. Courbet distributes that space among mourners without appointing a commanding hero. The open grave brings the ceremony to the foreground as a physical fact. The subject's scale is therefore social as well as pictorial: ordinary people receive life-size treatment without being remade as ideal figures.

works.title: The Gleaners
works.credit: Jean-François Millet. Des glaneuses ou Les glaneuses. Image credit: Jean-François Millet; Source credit: Google Arts & Culture — GgHsT2RumWxbtw. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The women collect what is left after the harvest, not the harvest itself. Millet makes that distinction visible by setting their handfuls against the abundance farther away. Their repeated bending connects the figures without turning them into interchangeable copies. The foreground gives exhausting, small-scale labour more pictorial weight than the larger operation in the distance.

works.title: The Angelus
works.credit: Jean-Francois Millet. L’Angélus. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The tools and basket remain beside the figures, so the prayer has the character of an interruption rather than a separate ceremony. Lowered heads turn attention towards the gap between the man and woman. The distant church places that private pause within a wider setting. Millet makes stillness legible through the work that has temporarily stopped.

works.title: Dance at the Moulin de la Galette
works.catalogueTitle: Bal du moulin de la Galette
works.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir. Bal du moulin de la Galette. Image credit: Sailko; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pierre_auguste_renoir,_ballo_del_moulin_del_la_galette,_1876,_01.JPG. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Light crosses the boundaries between people. Its scattered patches touch faces, clothing and ground, connecting separate conversations and dancing couples without requiring a single main event. The seated foreground offers points of entry into the crowd; farther back, attention disperses. Renoir's gathering remains sociable partly because no one figure claims the whole picture.

works.title: The Floor Scrapers
works.credit: Gustave Caillebotte. The Parquet Planers (The Floor Scrapers). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The floorboards set the direction of the work. Their long strips pull attention into the room, while the kneeling men move across them at different stages of the same task. Light from the window distinguishes scraped wood and bare backs. Caillebotte gives manual labour a measured setting without concealing the awkward bodily positions that it requires.

works.title: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1: The Artist's Mother
works.catalogueTitle: Arrangement in Grey and Black No.1, Portrait of the Artist's Mother
works.credit: James Abbott McNeill Whistler. Arrangement in Grey and Black No.1, Portrait of the Artist's Mother. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The title asks for attention to an arrangement as well as a person. Large areas of grey and black establish the portrait before the smaller pale accents of face, cap and hands become distinct. The framed picture and patterned curtain help divide the wall. These decisions do not cancel the sitter's presence; they give her quiet profile its unusually firm setting.

works.title: The Dance Class
works.credit: Edgar Degas. The Ballet Class. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: A dance class contains much more than dancing. Some figures practise, while others wait, rest or adjust their clothes. The open floor gives these small activities room to remain separate, even as the instructor and lesson hold the group together. Degas treats disciplined performance as the product of uneven attention, repetition and intervals between movements.

works.title: Starry Night over the Rhône
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. La Nuit étoilée. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: Two kinds of light occupy the night: scattered stars above and the city's long reflections below. The distinction keeps sky and river separate even where their colours approach one another. Near the bank, the couple supplies a scale against which the broad water can be understood. The scene is expansive, but it retains a place for two small figures.

works.title: The Church at Auvers
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. L’église d’Auvers-sur-Oise, vue du chevet. Image credit: Sailko; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vincent_Van_Gogh,_la_chiesa_di_auvers-sur-oise,_1890,_01.JPG. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The paths divide around the church, offering routes past a building whose outlines seem less stable than its masonry should allow. Walls bend beneath the deep blue sky; the small walking figure belongs to a different scale of movement. Van Gogh keeps the church recognisable while drawing its contours into the surrounding landscape's activity.

works.title: Dr Paul Gachet
works.credit: Vincent van Gogh. Le Docteur Paul Gachet. Image credit: GFreihalter; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Paris_7e_Mus%C3%A9e_d%E2%80%99Orsay_Van_Gogh_%C3%A0_Auvers-sur-Oise_981.jpg. CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Gachet's hand supports his head rather than making a gesture towards someone else. Sloping shoulders and the diagonal body repeat that downward pressure, while the flowers beside him hold a more upright position. Weariness is a plausible reading of the pose. It does not establish a medical condition or supply a diagnosis of the sitter.

works.title: The Card Players
works.credit: Paul Cezanne. Les Joueurs de cartes. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The bottle establishes a vertical division without making the two men mirror images. Their different postures settle on either side of the narrow table, with attention directed towards the cards rather than the viewer. Cézanne finds a sustained subject in that concentration. Little needs to happen for the balance between the figures to remain worth examining.

works.title: Apples and Oranges
works.credit: Paul Cézanne. Pommes et oranges. Image credit: Sailko; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Paul_c%C3%A9zanne,_mele_e_arance,_1899_ca._01.JPG. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The fruit appears solid even though the table is difficult to reconstruct as a single, consistent surface. Plates, folds and the raised dish introduce competing angles. Rather than treating those shifts simply as faulty perspective, follow how each gives an object more room to be seen. Cézanne's arrangement holds together through local relationships rather than one fixed viewpoint.

works.title: Arearea
works.credit: Paul Gauguin. Arearea. Image credit: Sailko; Own work. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Paul_gauguin,_arearea,_1892,_01.JPG. CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Full-frame proportional resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The red dog makes it difficult to mistake this setting for a neutral report of what Gauguin saw. Bands of colour organise the ground around the seated women; smaller figures occupy another register behind them. Simplification gives the scene coherence, but it also declares the painter's intervention. The work should not stand in for an unmediated account of Tahitian life.

works.title: Tahitian Women
works.credit: Paul Gauguin. Femmes de Tahiti. WikiArt: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop.
works.description: The two seated women have different directions of attention. One turns sideways while the other faces outward, so their closeness does not become a matched pose. Broad outlines and the restricted depth give their bodies weight. Hands and patterned clothing provide smaller distinctions within that compact arrangement, keeping the pair from becoming merely a repeated shape.

works.title: Portrait of Edma Pontillon
works.credit: Berthe Morisot. Portrait of Edma Pontillon. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/berthe-morisot/portrait-of-edma-pontillon
works.description: Dark clothing could make the seated figure seem like a single block, but Morisot separates hands, face and dress through small changes of light. The slight turn of the head counters the hands resting together. Pale patterned furnishings give those restrained movements a setting. The portrait's specificity depends on such adjustments rather than a conspicuous gesture.

works.title: Portrait of Émile Zola
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Portrait of Emile Zola. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/edouard-manet/portrait-of-emile-zola-1868
works.description: The open book and images on the wall make looking and reading part of the portrait's subject. They surround Zola without dissolving his sharply drawn profile into an inventory of interests. Manet holds the physical sitter and the intellectual setting in the same frame. The objects invite attention, but they do not explain everything about the person.

works.title: Frédéric Bazille Painting the Heron
works.catalogueTitle: Frederic Bazille Painting The Heron (Frederic Bazille at his Easel)
works.credit: Frederic Bazille Painting The Heron (Frederic Bazille at his Easel). WikiArt; Pierre-Auguste Renoir. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Bazille is occupied with making an image rather than presenting himself for one. The side view lets his leaning body, brush and nearby materials define the activity. Renoir turns a colleague's ordinary working posture into the basis of a portrait. Professional identity appears through a task in progress, not through a formal declaration of status.

works.title: Juan Prim, 8 October 1868
works.credit: Henri Regnault. Juan Prim, October 8, 1868. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-regnault/juan-prim-october-8-1868-1868
works.description: The raised foreleg prevents the horse from becoming a static platform beneath Prim. Its restless movement makes the rider's composure more conspicuous, while people and flags locate the scene beyond the immediate pair. Regnault uses a familiar form of public authority, the equestrian portrait, but its effect depends on keeping the animal visibly active.

closingSections.title: Compare kinds of attention
paragraphs: Place the card players beside Degas's dancers, or Bazille at work beside Zola reading. Concentration, waiting and self-presentation each produce a different kind of portrait. These comparisons are more useful than treating every work as a step towards a single modern style. Check the museum's current information before visiting: a selection from its holdings does not guarantee that every painting is on display.
